newsitem.title: USA: No int'l market upheaval seen from euro - Dini.
newsitem.headline: No int'l market upheaval seen from euro - Dini.

text.p: Italy's Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said Monday he saw no upheaval in international markets from the creation of the European single currency.
But Dini also warned that a weak European currency was not the solution to Europe's slow growth and high unemployment.

"It is clear that exchange rate depreciation is not the answer to European problems of low growth and high unemployment," Dini said in a speech prepared for the World Economy Laboratory Conference here.

The answer, rather, lay in "much greater competition in the markets for goods and services, including financial services, much more flexibility in labor markets, much ligher welfare state and lower taxes on both capital and labor."

Dini, a former treasurer and prime minister, also said that after the creation of the Euro, scheduled for January 1, 1999, for at least a first group of countries, interest rates should remain low on both sides of the Atlantic.

Dini said "a weak external value of the euro does not appear realistic" because the new European Central Bank would want to establish its credibility and because the policy mix is likely to be very similar in the US and Europe.

If the US succeeded in balancing its budget by 2002 as promised and the European countries remain committed to growth and stability, "monetary policy should have room to maintain relatively low interest rates on both sides of the Atlantic."
Dini said the creation of the European single currency would not cause upheaval in international markets but saw gradual portfolio shifts supporting the new currency in the long run.
